svg.title: Keep Operating Costs Separate From Recovery Volume
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-reported-operating-expenses; chapter number: 2; title: Keep Operating Costs Separate From Recovery Volume; subtitle: Reported mailing, document, notarization, and judicial-work expenses have different purchase units.; caption: Eric Richardson's student on Money Making Juggernaut reports mailing costs. Greg of Overage Acquisition reports a deed-copy cost, Nick Fullmer reports remote notarization, and Bob Diamond reports a judicial-work budget.; assumptions note: Each entry is a quoted point amount, so its bounds and reference value are identical. These are not market distributions or independently established typical prices. Approximate quotes remain approximate.; note: Richardson's student's letter and campaign figures describe the same mailing economics at different quantities and must not be added together. Diamond's legal budget is not a list-purchase cost.; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: USD per stated purchase or budget; bars: label: Student's single letter; min: 0.85; max: 0.85; typical: 0.85; display: $0.85 per letter; label: Student's mailing campaign; min: 850; max: 850; typical: 850; display: $850 for 1,000 letters; label: Greg's online grant-deed copy; min: 4; max: 4; typical: 4; display: About $4 per copy; label: Fullmer's remote notarization; min: 25; max: 25; typical: 25; display: $25 for the reported affidavit notarization; label: Diamond's judicial-work budget; min: 2500; max: 2500; typical: 2500; display: $2,500 reported legal-work budget
